idiom_name: generic Map/WeakMap wrapper with typed hit-or-miss API; TTL policy hand-written
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds types, not runtime: a cache is a Map<K, V> (or WeakMap<object, V>) behind a small generic class, and the compiler enforces the parts that matter - K extends object stops primitives from being weakly held, a V | undefined return documents miss semantics, and the interface can be swapped for a third-party store without touching callers. Eviction, TTL and invalidation remain application code; the same code runs in the browser tab and on the Node process, so an unbounded module-scope Map is a process-lifetime leak unless a bound is enforced. The classic cache object is replaced by a typed container plus policy, not by a language primitive.
pitfalls: get() returning undefined for a stored undefined value collapses hit and miss; use has() or a NullObject sentinel when V includes undefined.
Date.now() is not monotonic: clock adjustments can freeze or prematurely expire entries, so use performance.now()/hrtime.
Types vanish at runtime: a WeakMap cannot be iterated, sized or cleared, so a typed weak cache can never be invalidated wholesale - decide the invalidation path before choosing the container.
module-scope caches survive hot reloads in dev only partially: module state is replaced, so in-flight hits and invalidation bookkeeping can diverge from the previous instance.
